I will do this year mostly the way I did last year, with a few small adjustments. I have 30 mu, and with wheat-maize rotation I cannot spread money too loose, because fertilizer, seed, pesticide, and water all cost real cash. I have farmed a long time, so I do not like changing too much at once. Around here, if wheat and maize fertilizer is too light, the crop shows it fast and yield drops, so I would rather put a bit extra than regret it later. Since I have well irrigation, I will keep wheat steady with a few waterings at key times, and maize I will water when it needs it in summer. For seed, I will use improved wheat and hybrid maize because I have seen these do better on neighbors' fields and on my own land too. Stevia is different from grain, but I will still keep it on the better-managed part of the land, use enough nitrogen to push leaf growth, and not be stingy on water. Because my farm is 30 mu, I also think about labor. Some family members work off-farm, so I will keep management simple, use rotary tillage where it saves time, and keep pesticide sprays to the main problem periods instead of running to the field every few days.
